stories.title: ILS raises $11m Series A co-led by Aquiline and BlackFin
stories.ltme_summary: ILS, the company behind the ProVision private funds platform, has raised an $11m Series A co-led by Aquiline and BlackFin, according to LegalTechTalk. The round will fund the opening of ILS's first US offices. The item is a short summary line.
stories.hook: ILS raises $11m Series A co-led by Aquiline and BlackFin to open first US offices

stories.title: Government amends Courts and Tribunals Bill
stories.ltme_summary: Sarah Sackman KC MP has announced government amendments to the Courts and Tribunals Bill. They would remove the power to add offences to the judge-alone trial list without primary legislation and require affirmative secondary legislation for any increase in magistrates' custodial powers. The Bill reaches Lords Report Stage on 1 December.
stories.hook: Government amends Courts and Tribunals Bill to limit judge-alone trial expansion and tighten magistrates' sentencing powers

stories.title: Supreme Court limits costs in environmental cases
stories.ltme_summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that Foodrise's challenge to the UK-Australia trade agreement is not an environmental case under the Aarhus Convention. Foodrise will therefore not get the £10,000 cap on adverse costs. Campaigners including Friends of the Earth and the Environmental Law Foundation criticised the outcome, though some welcomed clarity on planning cases.
stories.hook: Supreme Court rules Foodrise's trade deal challenge falls outside Aarhus costs cap, removing £10,000 protection

stories.title: Government announces limits on NDAs
stories.ltme_summary: The government has announced restrictions on NDAs that stop victims of crime and workplace harassment being silenced, to take effect in January 2027. Victims of crime may speak about their experiences regardless of any NDA, and confidentiality clauses in new employer NDAs will be void where harassment occurs. Further proposals on harassment outside the workplace are due in 2027.
stories.hook: Government to void workplace NDA confidentiality clauses for harassment from January 2027

stories.title: Police trial digital drone identification
Scottish law firm launches specialist translation law practice
stories.ltme_summary: Scottish firm Inksters has launched Translation Law, which it believes is the first service of its kind internationally. The practice will examine the legal consequences of errors in human and AI translation and help lawyers challenge unreliable translations. Developed by John O'Shea and Deborah do Carmo, the service is described by founder Brian Inkster as addressing risks as firms adopt AI. A practical guide is due from Law Brief Publishing in early 2027.
stories.hook: Inksters launches Translation Law, a practice addressing liability for AI and human mistranslation in legal documents

stories.title: Sidley strengthens presence in London
SRA reaffirms its position on abuse of power by those that it regulates
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Regulation Authority has restated its position that a range of behaviours can amount to abuse of power by those it regulates. Named examples include misuse of litigation, SLAPPs, intimidating witnesses and whistleblowers, and improper use of non-disclosure agreements. SRA chief executive Sarah Rapson says acting in a client's best interests does not justify silencing people. The statement brings together earlier guidance, warning notices and public statements, all of which remain in force.
stories.hook: SRA says acting in a client's best interests never justifies silencing people, naming SLAPPs and misused NDAs as misconduct

stories.title: SRA's position on the abuse of power by the profession
stories.ltme_summary: The SRA has published a formal position statement on the abuse of power by the profession. It lists sexual harassment, bullying, misuse of litigation, SLAPPs, witness intimidation and improper NDAs as conduct that may lead to enforcement. The statement says no circumstances justify arguing that a duty to the client excuses abuse of power, and restates the SRA's commitment to pursuing misconduct.
stories.hook: SRA states there are no circumstances where a duty to the client justifies abuse of power, including SLAPPs and NDAs

stories.title: SEC Targets Elder-Investor Abuse in Settled Case Against Former Texas Adviser
Are You Ready for the Handover?
Virginia and Oregon Sue SpaceX, Alleging It Misled Users About Grok's Safeguards
The Playbook Strategy: A Step-By-Step Guide For Planning Your Conference Success!
Biglaw Associates Fishing For Raises Just Got A Bite
What One Women’s Health Advocate Is Watching After The Midterms
Walton Launches ‘Autonomous’ Transaction System
stories.ltme_summary: Walton, a US legal AI start-up, has launched what it calls an autonomous transaction system. It builds a customised execution graph from a firm's past precedents, with legal engineers working alongside attorneys. Walton says attorneys remain responsible for strategy and final review. Backed by Afore Capital, the company names Elego Law as an early access partner using the system in its venture financing practice.
stories.hook: Walton launches autonomous transaction system built from firms' precedents, with Elego Law as early access partner

stories.title: Simmons & Simmons Launches Lex-Ray Legislation Tool
stories.ltme_summary: Simmons & Simmons has launched Lex-Ray, an AI-powered platform surfacing UK and EU legislation with linked definitions, cross-references and amendment history. It offers an API and Model Context Protocol integration so AI tools can retrieve provisions. Partner Rich Folsom says it is available now to lawyers and compliance teams, and free for law students.
stories.hook: Simmons & Simmons launches Lex-Ray, an AI legislation platform with API access for AI tools

stories.title: Ex-Goodwin Lawyers Raise $11m For Funds Startup
stories.ltme_summary: ILS, the company behind the ProVision funds platform, has raised an additional $11m in a Series A co-led by Aquiline and BlackFin Capital Partners. ProVision automates side letter management and fund workflows for law firms and GPs. Co-founders include lawyers Fergus Plant and Jack McCarthy, previously associates at Goodwin, and CTO Stefano Benigni. Total funding since launch is $15m.
stories.hook: ILS raises $11m for ProVision, taking its funding to $15m with side letter automation for funds law

stories.title: Conclusive Will Review Your Legal AI Claims ‘Slop’
stories.ltme_summary: Conclusive, a legal AI clinic regulated by the SRA, has launched to offer fixed-fee litigation help for small businesses and individuals on claims between £10,000 and £100,000. Founder Jessica Fitzgerald says every claim begins with a solicitor call and that its review engine checks AI-drafted documents. The firm says it runs on Anthropic's Claude, with CoCounsel and LEAP AI tools also used.
stories.hook: Conclusive launches fixed-fee litigation clinic that reviews AI-drafted claims, running on Anthropic's Claude

stories.title: Document Drafter Hires Tech Pro In New Chief Evangelist Role
Skadden Adds Real Estate Partner in London
Why Truck Accident Claims Involve More Moving Parts Than Car Crashes
Construction Defects in South Florida: How Claims Start and Where They Stall
Dividing Property in a Texas Divorce: Community Assets, Separate Assets and Everything Between
How to Preserve Traffic Camera and Dashcam Evidence After a Rapid City Car Accident
How Much Is a Locked-In Syndrome Lawsuit Really Worth?
Energy giants set to cut legal spend as L500 reveals the top firms for client satisfaction
stories.ltme_summary: Legal 500 research of 10,000 GCs and corporate counsel in the US finds energy majors, including BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies and Shell, plan to cut overall legal spend. More than half of energy respondents expect to reduce spend, while M&A, tax and corporate advice are set to rise. Gibson Dunn, Latham & Watkins, Paul Hastings and Hogan Lovells Cadwalader comment on the findings.
stories.hook: Energy majors plan to cut overall legal spend while raising M&A and tax advice budgets, Legal 500 data shows

stories.title: Big changes could be coming to the SQE. Do they go far enough?
Beyond the transaction: Why Source of Funds and Wealth reviews need a wider view
stories.ltme_summary: eCOS by InfoTrack has enhanced its Verification of Funds report with AI-powered document analysis that flags inconsistencies between client information and evidence. A new Wealth Timeline and a VOF Update Service allow solicitors to rerun reports and keep an update log. The piece is sponsored content for Legal Futures.
stories.hook: eCOS by InfoTrack adds AI-powered Wealth Timeline and update service to its Verification of Funds report

stories.title: How managed IT services reduce cyber risk for law firms
stories.ltme_summary: Extech Cloud managing director Andrew Hookway argues that managed IT services can lower cyber risk for law firms through patching, access reviews, Microsoft 365 monitoring and incident response. The article links this to Cyber Essentials certification and to SRA expectations on client data. It is a sponsored commentary piece from the vendor.
stories.hook: Extech Cloud argues managed IT services can cut law firm cyber risk, tying the case to Cyber Essentials

stories.title: The 2027 risk register: five risks law firms shouldn’t carry into the new year
stories.ltme_summary: Piers Winton of Gallagher sets out five risk areas for law firms to review before 2027, including client money controls, AI accountability, governance during growth, operational resilience and insurance. He cites SRA warnings on AI, which received 42 reports of possible misuse between July 2025 and July 2026, and LPM research. The piece is commentary from a broker.
stories.hook: Gallagher's Piers Winton urges firms to review five risks for 2027, led by client money controls and AI oversight

stories.title: When AI becomes your confidant: chatbot advice and English law
Cloud-native legal software: what it means and why it matters
stories.ltme_summary: Tessaract's Mike Hinchliffe explains the difference between cloud-based and cloud-native legal practice management software. He argues cloud-native design gives better integrations, flexible growth, faster updates and a stronger base for AI. The article is vendor commentary promoting Tessaract's platform.
stories.hook: Tessaract argues cloud-native practice management, not simply hosted software, gives firms a stronger base for AI

stories.title: Sidley lands Weil's PE heavyweights in 10-partner London hire
PI specialist reports massive rise in profits
stories.ltme_summary: Minster Law's accounts for the year to 30 June show pre-tax profit up 97 per cent to £6.9m on turnover up 27 per cent to £54m. The firm is owned by BHL Holdings and has acquired ARAG Law's personal injury business. CEO Shirley Woolham says it is building for automation and AI, with less human involvement.
stories.hook: Minster Law profit almost doubles to £6.9m as it plans automation and AI to reduce human involvement

stories.title: Sidley swoops for 25 Weil Gotshal London lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: Sidley Austin has hired 25 London lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges, including Weil's former London managing partner, Jonathan Wood, and private equity co-head Marco Compagnoni. A further 15 cross-practice lawyers are moving from Weil, and the firm says its London headcount has grown 50 per cent in two years. Weil is winding down after senior partner departures and failed merger talks.
stories.hook: Sidley hires 25 London lawyers from winding-down Weil, Gotshal, led by former managing partner Jonathan Wood

stories.title: Courts given power to evict domestic abusers
stories.ltme_summary: Domestic abuse protection orders are now being rolled out across England and Wales after a two-year pilot in Greater Manchester, parts of London, Cleveland and North Wales involving 3,000 victims. Courts can impose any requirement needed to protect victims, including social media restrictions and treatment programmes. The Ministry of Justice and Law Society president Brett Dixon commented on the rollout.
stories.hook: Domestic abuse protection orders go national in England and Wales, after a pilot involving 3,000 victims

stories.title: Jury trials: government retreats on Henry VIII powers
stories.ltme_summary: Courts and legal services minister Sarah Sackman KC MP says the government will require primary legislation to add offences to the judge-alone trial list. Magistrates' sentencing increases will need affirmative secondary legislation and a Commons vote. The bill reaches Lords Report Stage on 1 December.
stories.hook: Government drops Henry VIII power to expand judge-only trials, requiring primary legislation for new offences

stories.title: Beyond the transaction: why Source of Funds and Wealth reviews need a wider view
stories.ltme_summary: Today's Conveyancer has published a piece on Source of Funds and Wealth reviews. The extract supplied is an unrelated UK Finance fraud headline, so the article's content cannot be confirmed. The headline suggests the piece argues that these checks need a wider view than the transaction alone.
stories.hook: Today's Conveyancer urges a wider view of source of funds and wealth reviews, though its text was not readable

McLaren Construction appoints two directors to board
SRA addresses abuse of power concerns
stories.ltme_summary: The SRA has restated its position on abuse of power, naming misuse of litigation, intimidatory tactics, SLAPPs, improper NDAs, sexual harassment and bullying as conduct falling short of its standards. Chief Executive Sarah Rapson says acting in a client's interests is no justification for silencing people. The SRA says the statement consolidates earlier guidance and warnings.
stories.hook: SRA chief Sarah Rapson says misuse of litigation and improper NDAs fall below professional standards

stories.title: Government proposes knife licensing scheme
Government expands electronic monitoring scheme
stories.ltme_summary: The Ministry of Justice says electronic monitoring tags will be fitted to offenders at 83 prisons by the end of March 2027, under a £100m investment. A three-month pilot at Croydon and Highbury Corner magistrates' courts will fit tags before court departure. The announcement does not set out detailed eligibility criteria.
stories.hook: Ministry of Justice extends tagging at source to 83 prisons and two London magistrates' courts

Will Higher Sales Taxes Drive Shoppers Out Of Los Angeles?
Nothing Says Lovin’ Like Raises
Which Is It: Do We Need To ‘Protect Our Geniuses’ Or Keep China From Outpacing Us On AI At All Costs?
Biglaw’s AI Shift Is Changing How Legal Work Gets Priced
stories.ltme_summary: Above the Law's daily quote feature carries comments from Anne-Marie Allgrove, Baker McKenzie's national managing partner in Australia, given to Lawyers Weekly. She says AI is changing how the firm delivers and prices work, with more alternative fee arrangements, and that hourly billing will no longer be the default across all mandates.
stories.hook: Baker McKenzie Australia says hourly billing will no longer be the default as AI reshapes pricing

stories.title: Firm Matching Original Special Bonus… Now That The Market Is Beating It
Akin AI Team Developing Tool For Funds Practice
'AI Sprawl': Firms Weigh How Much AI Is Too Much
AI News – Simmons & Simmons first law firm to meet global AI industry standard
stories.ltme_summary: Simmons & Simmons says it is the first law firm to meet the LTC4 global AI industry standard, with more than 1,700 lawyers and staff holding the LTC4 'Working with AI' certification. The competency, launched earlier in 2026 by the Legal Technology Core Competencies Certification Coalition, sets out responsible AI use in firms, covering human oversight, verification and confidentiality. The firm's global managing partner Emily Monastiriotis describes the certification as central to its AI-enabled strategy.
stories.hook: Simmons & Simmons says 1,700 staff now hold LTC4's 'Working with AI' certification, making it the first firm to meet the standard

Forbes’ Top AI Lawyers: Who’s Winning the Race to Become America’s Legal AI Elite
stories.ltme_summary: Forbes has published its first America's Top Lawyers for AI list, naming 50 attorneys across six practice areas. LawFuel reports that advisory and litigation account for 41 places, nine honourees practise at litigation boutiques, and women hold 18 places, or 36 per cent. The list names lawyers at Latham & Watkins, Gibson Dunn, Keker, Van Nest & Peters and others.
stories.hook: Forbes' first AI lawyers ranking puts nine litigation boutique practitioners among 50 honourees

stories.title: David Seymour accused of ‘betraying Kiwi voters’ over his push to scrap six-month assisted dying limit
Law firm collapses and the peril of large SRA fines
stories.ltme_summary: Kingsley Napley partners Iain Miller and Stephen Nelson argue in a Legal Futures guest post that the SRA should review its fining policy after the wind-down of Weil, Gotshal & Manges. They note the SRA can fine lawyer-owned firms up to £25,000, can fine ABSs up to £250m, and has devised a turnover-based model permitting fines of up to 5 per cent of turnover, which they say can be disproportionate.
stories.hook: Kingsley Napley says the SRA's turnover-based fining model risks destroying firms, citing the Weil wind-down

stories.title: MPs: SRA not equipped to restrain oppressive litigation by solicitors
stories.hook: Justice committee says the SRA lacks the powers and rules to police solicitors' oppressive litigation

stories.title: Leading law firm launches its own source of funds AI tool
stories.ltme_summary: Keystone Law has launched Origin, an in-house source of funds tool that uses AI agents to guide clients through source of funds enquiries and compile a documented report for the lawyer. Money laundering reporting officer Luke Haddon says it was introduced in the conveyancing department in September and rolled out firm-wide. Keystone has no plans to sell it to other firms.
stories.hook: Keystone Law builds Origin, an AI source of funds tool it says has no equivalent on the market

stories.title: Sanction for barrister’s antisemitic posts “appears lenient”, says BSB chair
stories.ltme_summary: The Bar Standards Board chair Professor Chris Bones says a four-month suspension given to barrister Forz Khan for antisemitic LinkedIn posts appears lenient. He says the BSB will decide on an appeal only after receiving the Bar disciplinary tribunal's written reasons. Shadow ministers Nick Timothy and Lord Wolfson had written to the BSB about the sanction.
stories.hook: BSB chair says four-month suspension of barrister Forz Khan appears lenient, but no appeal until reasons arrive

stories.hook: Bar Council and BSB propose 3.5 per cent practising certificate fee rise for 2027-28

McCormick Offers to Sell Colman’s to Avoid Full UK Investigation Into Unilever Deal

The three cases are Round Hill, Reservoir and ABG.

stories.source_name: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

seen_in.source_name: ChatGPT Is Eating the World (Edward Lee)

stories.ltme_summary: Edward Lee's blog reports that the two AI copyright suits against Uncharted Labs, brought by UMG Recordings and Justice, have been reassigned to Judge Jeannette Vargas after the death of Judge Alvin Hellerstein in late October. Hellerstein's one major decision in the cases, on DMCA anti-circumvention claims, has been cited by other courts.

stories.title: Product webinar - Legora for litigation: unlocking Fact Intelligence
stories.ltme_summary: Legora is promoting a live product webinar on Fact Intelligence for litigation teams, which builds source-linked chronologies and surfaces conflicting accounts. Gregory Mostyn and Kyle Poe will run a demo on 8 December 2026 for EMEA and AMER audiences, with an APAC session on 9 December.
stories.hook: Legora schedules a December webinar on Fact Intelligence for source-linked litigation chronologies

stories.title: Fact Intelligence | Legora
stories.ltme_summary: Legora is promoting a live webinar on 8 and 9 December about Fact Intelligence, a product that builds a structured factual record from case documents for litigation teams. The page is vendor marketing.

stories.title: Email Workflow Automation for Legal Teams: Govern It First
stories.ltme_summary: Neota Logic argues that legal email workflow automation should separate deterministic rules from AI drafting and classification, with logged steps and human checkpoints. It cites the Alabama State Bar's FO-2026-01 opinion and the State Bar of California's May 2026 guidance on agentic systems and access controls.
stories.hook: Neota Logic argues AI should draft and classify legal email, while rules make the decisions

stories.title: AI in Contract Management | Summize
stories.ltme_summary: Summize, a contract management vendor, has published an explainer on AI contract management. It describes seven uses across the contract lifecycle, including data extraction, playbook checks, risk scoring and redlining. It cites WorldCC research that businesses lose an average of 9 per cent of contract value through value erosion.
stories.hook: Summize's guide to AI contract management cites WorldCC finding of 9 per cent contract value erosion

stories.title: Auckland Lawyer’s Costly Lesson in Overseas Investment Law
stories.ltme_summary: The Lawyers and Conveyancers Disciplinary Tribunal has found Auckland commercial lawyer Andrew Jarvis grossly negligent over advice enabling overseas investors to buy 271 hectares of forestry land without required consent. The tribunal did not find professional misconduct. Jarvis had earlier been ordered to pay $275,000 in civil penalties by the High Court in February 2025.
stories.hook: New Zealand tribunal finds lawyer Andrew Jarvis grossly negligent over overseas investment consents

stories.title: Bell Gully Reclaims IFLR’s New Zealand Crown, but Where Was Chapman Tripp?
stories.hook: Bell Gully wins IFLR's New Zealand law firm award, its fourth since 2020

stories.title: Weil Built the AI But Its Partners Didn’t Stay to Use It
stories.ltme_summary: LawFuel comments on the wind-down of Weil, Gotshal & Manges and what happens to its AI tools. It recalls Weil's August announcement of BenchMark, a litigation tool built with Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise for Legal. Weil lawyers who have left include Jonathon Soler, now at Gibson Dunn, and Ramona Nee, now at Kirkland & Ellis. Crosby, Scissero and Vetta have made bids for parts of the firm's assets.
stories.hook: LawFuel asks who will own Weil's BenchMark litigation tool as its departing partners take the know-how

The extract instead shows an unrelated headline about a Supreme Court ruling on a boat storage easement over a car park, so the FCA statement itself cannot be confirmed from this text.

The strategic risk leader: building the capabilities that define the next decade in consulting
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp argues that risk leaders at consulting firms will need portfolio-level exposure visibility, auditability of conflicts decisions, enforced information barriers and governance of AI agents. It says clients increasingly ask firms to demonstrate conflicts processes and that Intapp Walls for AI extends barriers to AI tools.
stories.hook: Intapp says consulting risk leaders must govern AI agents and prove conflicts processes to clients

stories.title: How Firm AI runs the business of law
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp describes its Firm AI approach to running the business of law, following a 10 November session. It says Finnegan uses Intapp DealCloud with Celeste for client and relationship data, and sets out four Celeste scenarios covering cross-sell, matter opening, timesheets and profitability.
stories.hook: Intapp says Celeste's Firm AI can run business functions for law firms, citing Finnegan's DealCloud use

stories.title: How Firm AI is changing the way investment banks find and win mandates
stories.ltme_summary: Intapp interviews its own team on Firm AI for investment banks, arguing that proprietary client data can be passively captured and used by LLMs through a deal-specific context engine. It says origination is where AI will have the biggest impact, and that Firm AI can help bankers identify companies likely to transact.
stories.hook: Intapp argues its Firm AI context engine can help investment banks win more mandates

stories.title: Pacific Northwest University
stories.ltme_summary: Mitratech's customer feed describes Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences, a non-profit university in Yakima Valley, Washington, using Insights for Perform to review departmental performance. The extract is a short summary and does not give the full deployment details.
stories.hook: Pacific Northwest University uses Mitratech Insights for Perform to review departments

stories.title: HighQ MCP: Bring your matter context to the AI tools you already use
stories.ltme_summary: Thomson Reuters says HighQ MCP is now available in Claude's connectors directory, joining ChatGPT and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Eligible users can connect their HighQ instance without admins setting up a custom connector. The read-only Model Context Protocol connection respects existing HighQ permissions.
stories.hook: Thomson Reuters adds Claude to HighQ MCP, alongside ChatGPT and Microsoft 365 Copilot
